claims.text: The target alloy system is NbMoCrTiAl.
High-energy planetary ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering produces an NbMoCrTiAl composite containing in situ TiC and Al2O3.
The composite contains approximately 32 vol.% TiC.
The composite contains approximately 7 vol.% Al2O3.
TiC and Al2O3 particles act as second-phase reinforcing agents in the NbMoCrTiAl matrix.
Second-phase strengthening contributes to the improved compressive strength.
The processing route causes grain refinement.
Grain refinement contributes to improved high-temperature compressive strength.
The reinforced composite has enhanced or superior high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast alloy.
The composite has improved stability under oxidative conditions.
The composite achieves a room-temperature compressive fracture strength of about 1542 MPa, approximately 50% above the as-cast alloy's 1010 MPa.
The approximately 50% strength improvement demonstrated at room temperature will translate into improved high-temperature mechanical performance.
The as-cast NbMoCrTiAl alloy has lower compressive strength than the powder-metallurgy composite.
The as-cast NbMoCrTiAl alloy has lower oxidation resistance than the powder-metallurgy composite.
NbMoCrTiAl has lower neutron-activation potential than conventional alloys because of its elemental makeup.
The reinforced NbMoCrTiAl composite is a promising low-activation structural material for fusion-reactor plasma-facing components.
The composite is more suitable than the as-cast alloy for plasma-facing components.
The claimed performance is expected to hold under the high-temperature, high-oxidation conditions typical of fusion plasma-facing components.
Irradiation-induced effects may create additional performance challenges.
The neutron-activation behavior of this material has not yet been definitively quantified.

contradictions.description: The as-cast alloy is labeled as the material's initial state, but elsewhere it is treated as a separate control or baseline against a composite fabricated by ball milling and spark plasma sintering. The stated powder-metallurgy route does not clearly begin from an as-cast NbMoCrTiAl specimen.
